claims.claim: Most people in the AI risk community think AI-caused doom is less likely than not.
claims.context: In fact, most people in the community think doom is less likely than not.

claims.claim: Geoffrey Hinton has said there is a 10-50% chance that AI drives humanity extinct.
claims.context: Geoffrey Hinton has said 10-50% chance.

claims.claim: Dario Amodei has said there is a 10-25% chance that AI drives humanity extinct.
claims.context: Dario Amodei has said 10-25%,

claims.claim: Elon Musk has said there is a 10-30% chance that AI drives humanity extinct.
claims.context: Elon Musk 10-30%,

claims.claim: In Katja Grace’s survey sample of 1,600 AI researchers, the average respondent assigned an 18% chance to AI driving humanity extinct.
claims.context: and the average AI researcher in Grace’s 1,600 person sample said 18%.

claims.claim: Some people hold more pessimistic views about AI-caused doom than the 10-30% range previously cited.
claims.context: There are some people who are more pessimistic;

claims.claim: Daniel Kokotajlo, co-author of AI 2027, says there is a 70-80% chance of AI-caused doom.
claims.context: my AI 2027 co-author Daniel Kokotajlo says 70-80%,

claims.claim: Eliezer Yudkowsky says there is a 90% or greater chance of AI-caused doom.
claims.context: and Eliezer Yudkowsky says 90%+.

claims.context: But both of these people have devoted their lives to fighting back,

claims.claim: The addressee falsely portrays the AI risk community as expecting a perfect omniscient omnipotent superintelligence that controls every atom in the universe.
claims.context: 2: You falsely portray the AI risk community as expecting a perfect omniscient omnipotent superintelligence that controls every atom in the universe.

claims.claim: The person being criticized wrote that AI risk arguments depend on the premise that humans can design an omniscient and omnipotent AI.
claims.context: “[These arguments] depend on the premises that humans are so gifted that they can design an omniscient and omnipotent AI” (source)

claims.claim: The person being criticized wrote that AI risk proponents assumed human engineers would grant AIs unlimited irreversible control over Earth’s physical infrastructure amounting to omnipotence over every atom.
claims.context: “They assumed that human engineers would grant [AIs] unlimited and irreversible control over the earth’s physical infrastructure, amounting to omnipotence over every atom on the planet.” (source)

claims.claim: The person being criticized wrote that psychometric general intelligence should not be confused with a mystical AI notion of omniscience and omnipotence.
claims.context: “Important not to confuse the notion of “general intelligence” from psychometrics … with the (somewhat mystical) notion bandied about in AI of omniscience and omnipotence.” (source)

claims.claim: The person being criticized wrote that AI will never be omniscient or omnipotent and that such ideas come from comic books or religion.
claims.context: “It will never be omniscient . . . it’ll never be omnipotent. That’s out of comic books or religion.” (source)

claims.claim: The person being criticized wrote that no system could learn the position and velocity of every particle in the universe, so no AI system can do anything or know everything.
claims.context: “There’s no system that could learn the position and velocity of every particle in the universe. So long as that is true, there can’t be an AI system that can do anything or know everything.” (source)

claims.claim: The person being criticized described foom, digital megalomania, instant omniscience, and perfect control of every molecule as fantasies to put aside.
claims.context: “When we put aside fantasies like foom, digital megalomania, instant omniscience, and perfect control of every molecule in the universe…” (source)

claims.claim: The person being criticized wrote that Artificial Superintelligence consists of perfect omniscience in a progression from animals to humans to AI.
claims.context: “From animals to dull humans to smart humans to AI to Artificial Superintelligence, the latter consisting of perfect omniscience.” (source)

claims.claim: The person being criticized made many more statements along the same lines about omniscience and omnipotence.
claims.context: …and many more statements along the same lines.

claims.context: But not only is this not our belief, but we try hard to explicitly specify that we believe the opposite.

passages.text: 5: You employ weird pseudo-arguments that could prove anything
claims: The critic employs weird pseudo-arguments that could prove anything.

passages.text: (source)
You argue that superintelligence is “meaningless” because “there’s no point at which it’s meaningful to say” that “yesterday we didn’t have superintelligence. Today we do have superintelligence.”
claims: The critic argues superintelligence is meaningless because there is no point where one can say superintelligence arrived from one day to the next.

passages.text: But this could disprove any concept.
For example:
Age is meaningless.
After all, there’s no point at which someone was young yesterday, but old today.
Height is meaningless.
After all, there is no specific line where one centimeter below the line is short, but one centimeter above the line is tall.
Lakes don’t exist.
After all, a puddle is not a lake.
But there is no point at which adding one extra drop of water to a non-lake turns it into a lake.
Several people with philosophical backgrounds commented that this was the sorites argument,

passages.text: If AI fully fizzled and the industry collapsed, we would be highly screwed.
The good news is I think that an industry collapse is highly unlikely.
Even if Mythos is close to the best that AIs will ever be, a year from now we will have cheaper and faster and more abundant Fable-level systems.
We will have swarms of Fable agents.
Demand will be high, and benefits will be higher.
That could end up being bad news for specific labs, but not in general.

What always worries me far more is that AI capabilities might advance faster than we can handle them, via recursive self-improvement, and potentially causing everyone to die as a side effect of the resulting systems.

passages.text: This was a decade where centuries happened.
